native_mcp_support.notes: Remote MCP Tools remain natively supported and are documented against grok-4.6. Configure with {type:'mcp', server_url, server_label, server_description, allowed_tools, authorization, headers}; xAI holds the MCP connection server-side. Docs (re-read 2026-08-19): 'Only Streaming HTTP and SSE transports are supported' (no stdio). Works with 'the xAI native SDK, the OpenAI compatible Responses API, and the Speech to Speech API'. 'The require_approval and connector_id parameters in the OpenAI Responses API are not currently supported.' Pricing page: MCP invocations are token-billed only — 'you will not be charged for the tool invocation but will be charged for any tokens used.'

skills_concept.notes: Still no API-level skills primitive. Grok Build (the CLI/TUI coding harness) documents skills as 'reusable folders containing markdown instructions, script files, and resources for agents', discovered from ./.grok/skills/ (walked to repo root), ~/.grok/skills/, enabled plugin directories and configured custom paths, with user-invocable skills exposed as /<skill-name> slash commands (progressive disclosure). These are CLI/product features, not developer-API primitives, and xAI publishes no token/context cost for them. Grok Bot (launched 2026-08-11, docs.x.ai/grok-bot/bots) is likewise a product-level 'durable AI teammate' surface, not an API skills mechanism.

context_window_tokens.notes: Model card: 'Context window: 500,000'. Pricing table also lists grok-4.6 at 500k. NOTE this is HALF of grok-4.3's 1M window — the flagship moved down in context while moving up in price, so an MCP tool surface occupies twice the share of the window it did on grok-4.3.

input_output_shared.notes: xAI does not state separate input/output pools; the OpenAI-compatible convention (one shared window) is implied and the model card publishes a single 'Context window' number. Medium confidence — not explicitly documented.

max_input_tokens.notes: No max-input cap is documented separately from the 500k window. Not derived, because no max-output figure is published to subtract.

max_output_tokens_default.notes: No default max-output value is published on the model card or in the API reference (checked 2026-08-19). max_tokens is accepted through the OpenAI-compatible surface but its default is not documented.

max_output_tokens_max.notes: No maximum single-completion cap is published. What binds is the 500k shared window; xAI documents no separate per-response numeric ceiling.

extended_context.notes: No beta/extended window beyond 500k. The 200k figure that appears in pricing is a LONG-CONTEXT PRICING threshold, not a window: 'Models with long context pricing bill the long context rates for all tokens in a request once its prompt reaches the model's long context threshold' (grok-4.6: >= 200k).

reasoning_tokens_count_as_output.notes: 'Reasoning tokens: Full completion token price' — reasoning tokens bill at the output rate and are reported via reasoning_tokens in usage. The reasoning docs add: 'reasoning_effort defaults to high. Reasoning cannot be disabled.'

tokenizer_public.notes: No public tokenizer library, HF repo or tiktoken base found as of 2026-08-19; no count-tokens endpoint in the API reference. Medium confidence: absence of documentation is not proof of absence.

tokenizer_access.notes: Closed for programmatic local use. The interactive Tokenizer Playground in the xAI console remains the only exploration path; no API and no library are documented.

count_tokens_method.notes: No count-tokens API endpoint documented (unlike OpenAI's token-counting endpoint or Google countTokens). image_token_rule.notes: Image input is supported but xAI publishes no image-to-token conversion rule (no tile/patch formula like OpenAI's). The image-understanding page (re-read 2026-08-19) documents only 'Maximum image size: 20MiB', 'Supported image file types: jpg/jpeg or png', and states there is no documented per-request numeric cap on the number of images — what binds is the 20MiB per-image size limit and the model's context window. audio_token_rule.notes: No audio input on the text models; speech is handled by the separate Voice / Speech-to-Speech API models. No audio token rule applies here.

skills_loading_model.notes: Not applicable at the API layer. The only Grok-side progressive disclosure is in the Grok Build CLI, where user-invocable skills appear as slash commands rather than being preloaded.

skills_context.system_prompt_overhead_notes: No fixed system-prompt overhead is documented; system-prompt tokens bill as input at $2.00/1M short-context ($0.50/1M if served from cache, $4.00/$1.00 under long-context pricing).

prompt_caching.notes: Prompt caching applies: cached prompt tokens are 'billed at the cached prompt token price, which is substantially lower than the regular prompt token price', and the pricing table lists a $0.50/1M cached-input rate for grok-4.6 ($1.00/1M long-context). Cache hits are reported via cached_tokens. NOTE grok-4.6's cache discount is shallower than grok-4.3's ($0.50 vs $0.20/1M, i.e. 25% of input vs 16%).

memory_feature.notes: No persistent cross-session memory is exposed by the API. Context Compaction (POST /v1/responses/compact, or chat.compact() in the SDK) can 'Shrink long conversations into an opaque compaction that can be reused in follow-up calls', but it is opt-in state management, not memory; multi-turn state otherwise rides on store_messages/previous_response_id or use_encrypted_content.

input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Short-context rate (prompt below the model's long-context threshold, 200k tokens). At/above the threshold LONG-context rates bill ALL tokens in the request: $4.00/1M input. grok-4.6 is 60% more expensive on input and 140% more expensive on output than grok-4.3.

output_per_mtok_usd.notes: Short-context output rate; long-context output rate is $12.00/1M once the prompt reaches the 200k long-context threshold.

cached_input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Cached-input rate; $1.00/1M under long-context pricing. Cached tokens still count toward the long-context threshold: 'Long context pricing applies when total prompt tokens (including cached tokens) exceed the model's long context threshold.'

batch_discount.notes: Pricing page batch section lists only 'grok-4.3, grok-4.20-0309-reasoning, grok-4.20-0309-non-reasoning, grok-4.20-multi-agent-0309' at 20% off and states 'Models not listed above have no batch discount.' grok-4.6 is therefore not batch-discounted. billing_unit.notes: Billed per token for model usage; built-in server-side tools add a separate per-invocation fee, while Remote MCP tools are 'Token-based only'.

cost.multimodal_billing_notes: Image input bills as input tokens; xAI publishes no tile/patch formula, so per-image cost must be measured empirically. Per-image ceiling is 20MiB, jpg/jpeg or png. No audio on this model.

reasoning_billed_as_output.notes: Prompt-caching usage-and-pricing page (re-read 2026-08-19) lists the billed token types: 'Prompt tokens (non-cached): Full prompt token price', 'Cached prompt tokens: Reduced cached prompt token price', 'Completion tokens: Full completion token price', 'Reasoning tokens: Full completion token price'. function_calling.notes: Model card capability: 'Function calling: Connect the xAI model to external tools and systems.' OpenAI-compatible tool format on both Chat Completions and the Responses API.

parallel_tool_calls.notes: Parallel function calling is enabled by default — the model may request multiple tool calls in a single response; disable with parallel_tool_calls: false. tool_choice accepts 'auto' | 'required' | 'none' | a named function.

max_tools_hard.notes: Function-calling guide, Tool Schema Reference, `name` field (re-read 2026-08-19): "Unique identifier (max 200 tools per request)". The sentence carries no model qualification, but grok-4.6 is the ONLY model named anywhere on that page, so 200 is asserted here and nowhere else in the xAI roster. SCOPE: AGGREGATE per request — custom function tools + built-in server-side tools + every tool exposed by every connected Remote MCP server share the same budget; no per-MCP-server cap is documented. CONFLICT (2026-08-19 final audit): the 200 figure is NOT corroborated as an API-wide platform limit. xAI's REST API reference documents a lower, equally unqualified number against the same `tools` array — "A list of tools the model may call in JSON-schema. Currently, only functions and web search are supported as tools. A max of 128 tools are supported." (https://docs.x.ai/developers/rest-api-reference/inference/chat). The models index and the per-model pages state no tool-count cap at all, the Remote MCP page names only grok-4.6, and there is no error-reference page (https://docs.x.ai/developers/error-reference returned 404 on 2026-08-19). Plan against 128, the lower of the two unqualified platform numbers. Confidence lowered high → medium (2026-08-19) because of that unresolved 200-vs-128 doc conflict; the grok-4.6 model page itself (https://docs.x.ai/developers/models/grok-4.6) states no tool-count limit.

max_tools_practical.notes: EMPIRICAL, NOT SPEC — xAI publishes no tool-count degradation figure. Midpoint of the cross-vendor 30–50 band reported by practitioners; the cited round-up (opened 2026-08-19) records Anthropic's '30–50 tools' guidance, OpenAI's 'fewer than 20 functions' soft suggestion, and a June 2026 584-tool study where flat routing accuracy fell 58.2% → 42.1% F1 going from 51 to 584 tools, with an ~10-point 'oracle ceiling' gap that shortlisting cannot close. No Grok-specific measurement exists. xAI's own mitigation guidance is allowed_tools: 'Reduce context overhead by limiting tool definitions the model needs to consider.' On grok-4.6 the 500k window (half of grok-4.3's) makes definition bloat bite sooner in context terms.

tool_definition_shape.notes: OpenAI-compatible {type:'function', name, description, parameters} tool objects; the OpenAI SDK works against the xAI base_url. Remote MCP tools are declared as {type:'mcp', server_url, server_label, ...}.

tool_defs_count_as_input.notes: Tool definitions are serialized into the request and billed as input tokens. Remote MCP docs: without allowed_tools 'all tool definitions exposed by the MCP server are automatically injected into the model's context', and allowed_tools exists to 'Reduce context overhead by limiting tool definitions the model needs to consider.' Pricing page confirms MCP tools are 'Token-based only' — no per-invocation fee, but every definition token is charged at the input rate.

tool_search_deferral.notes: No progressive tool disclosure / tool-search mechanism is documented. allowed_tools is a static per-request allow-list chosen by the caller, not runtime deferral; there is no xAI equivalent of Claude's tool-search / defer_loading. Re-checked the tools overview and remote-MCP pages on 2026-08-19.

max_tool_name_len.notes: No character limit on tool/function names is documented — the schema reference lists name as a required string ('Unique identifier (max 200 tools per request)') with no length constraint, and publishes no equivalent to OpenAI's 64-character cap. Remote MCP tool names additionally carry a '<server_label>.' prefix for tool-call prefixing, with no documented cap on the combined length.

max_tool_description_len.notes: Tool description length carries no documented numeric limit; description is required ('What the tool does — helps the model decide when to use it') with no character or token limit stated. What binds in practice is the 500k context window.

max_request_size.notes: No maximum request payload size (bytes/MB) is published anywhere in the docs — checked the API reference, function-calling, remote-MCP, tools-overview and rate-limit pages on 2026-08-19. The only published payload ceiling is per-image ('Maximum image size: 20MiB'). What binds a request is the 500k context window and the tokens-per-minute rate limit.

max_tool_result_size.notes: Tool result/output size carries no documented numeric limit. Server-side tool output is consumed inside xAI's agentic loop; client-side function results are appended to the conversation as strings with no stated size limit, so what binds is the 500k context window.

max_parallel_tool_calls_count.notes: No numeric cap on how many tool calls the model may emit in one response is documented. Parallel calling is on by default and can be switched off with parallel_tool_calls: false; max_turns limits assistant turns, and explicitly 'does not directly limit the number of individual tool calls'.

tool_use_per_turn_limit.notes: max_turns bounds the agentic loop, not tool calls: 'max_turns does not directly limit the number of individual tool calls. Instead, it limits the number of assistant turns in the agentic loop.' 'If max_turns is not specified, the server applies a global default cap' — xAI does not publish that default's value. max_turns only counts assistant/server-side turns within one request; a client-side tool call returns control to the caller and the next request starts with a fresh turn counter.

max_connected_servers.notes: No numeric cap on simultaneous Remote MCP server connections per request is documented; the multi-server example wires three servers (distinct server_url/server_label) in one request with no stated ceiling. The limits that actually bind are AGGREGATE: the 200-tool per-request cap covering every connected server's tools plus any custom functions and built-in tools, and the 500k context window.

max_total_tools.notes: The 200-tool per-request cap IS the aggregate ceiling for grok-4.6: xAI documents no separate "tools across all servers" limit, so custom function tools + built-in server-side tools + every tool exposed by every connected MCP server are counted against the same 200. Scope: aggregate per request, not per MCP server. Asserted only for grok-4.6 because that is the only model the citing page names. CONFLICT (2026-08-19 final audit): the 200 figure is NOT corroborated as an API-wide platform limit. xAI's REST API reference documents a lower, equally unqualified number against the same `tools` array — "A list of tools the model may call in JSON-schema. tools_mcp.tool_schema_limits_notes: Function-calling schema reference (re-read 2026-08-19): name = 'Unique identifier (max 200 tools per request)'; description = 'What the tool does — helps the model decide when to use it'; parameters = 'JSON Schema defining function inputs'. Root-schema rule was WIDENED since the 2026-06-21 snapshot: the parameters root must be an object, but 'A root anyOf or oneOf also works when every branch is itself an object'; a root that is a scalar, an array, or an anyOf/oneOf with a non-object branch is 'rejected with a 400 error'. No documented depth, property-count or enum-size limits. Remote MCP tools are prefixed by server_label ('A label to identify the server (used for tool call prefixing)'). Without allowed_tools, 'all tool definitions exposed by the MCP server are automatically injected into the model's context'. grok-4.6 supports reasoning effort low/medium/high(default)/xhigh; xhigh is grok-4.6-and-later only.
tools_mcp.other_limits_notes: Remote MCP: Streaming HTTP and SSE transports only (no stdio); require_approval and connector_id from the OpenAI Responses API are not supported. Server-side built-in tool invocation fees (pricing page, 2026-08-19): web_search $5/1k calls, x_search $5/1k calls, code_execution $5/1k calls, attachment_search $10/1k calls, collections_search $2.50/1k calls; Remote MCP tools are 'Token-based only'. Only successfully executed server-side tools are billed (server_side_tool_usage), not every attempted call. Priority processing (service_tier: 'priority') bills all token types at 2x standard rates. Context Compaction is OPT-IN (corrected 2026-08-19): it is an explicit call to POST /v1/responses/compact or chat.compact(), not automatic. max_turns caps assistant/server-side turns in the agentic loop and 'If max_turns is not specified, the server applies a global default cap' whose value xAI does not publish. Rate limits (2026-08-19): 150 requests/second and 50M tokens/minute at Tier 0, rising to 500 RPS / 100M TPM at Tier 4 — roughly 4x grok-4.3's throughput. Regions us-east-1 and us-west-2. grok-4.6 is NOT batch-discount eligible. Long-context pricing starts at a 200k prompt and re-rates the entire request.

strict_function_schema.notes: No OpenAI-style strict function-schema mode is documented. The only schema constraint xAI publishes is the parameters-root rule (object, or anyOf/oneOf whose branches are all objects); no 100-property / 5-depth / no-oneOf enforcement mode exists.

models.notes: Current xAI flagship, GA 2026-08-12 and the only model with a stated knowledge cutoff (2026-02-01) on the models page. For MCP work the trade is explicit: 500k window (vs grok-4.3's 1M) at $2/$6 per 1M (vs $1.25/$2.50), with the same documented 200-tool aggregate per-request cap and no batch discount. Reasoning cannot be disabled (reasoning_effort defaults to 'high'; xhigh available), so every request carries reasoning tokens billed at the output rate — a real cost factor for tool-heavy agent loops. Context Compaction (opt-in, POST /v1/responses/compact) is the documented lever for long MCP sessions.

output_per_mtok_usd.notes: Short-context output rate; long-context output rate is $5.00/1M once the prompt reaches the 200k long-context threshold.
